Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

SurveyNCD 0.2.0

New features

  • Survey design helpers dhs_design(), mics_design() and steps_design() build the design from each programme’s standard variable names (DHS: PSU v021, strata v023, weight v005 / 1e6).
  • survey_prevalence(): design-based prevalence of any number of binary indicators, overall or by one or more grouping variables, with design effects.
  • mm_prevalence() now also accepts a survey design object, supports several by variables and excludes missing scores by domain estimation (same estimates as before for complete designs).
  • multimorbidity_index(threshold = ) sets the number of conditions defining multimorbidity (e.g. 3 for complex multimorbidity) and adds mm_multimorbid.
  • mm_patterns(): prevalence of condition pairs/triads with observed-to-expected ratios.
  • mm_standardize() and who_standard_population(): direct age standardisation to the WHO World Standard Population, with design-based SEs.
  • mm_bounds(): sensitivity bounds for “don’t know” answers.
  • survey_concentration_index() gains type = "generalized", "erreygers" and "wagstaff", bounds, and by for group-wise indices.
  • survey_concentration_curve() and survey_slope_index() (slope and relative index of inequality).
  • ncd_table(): publication-ready prevalence tables.
  • autoplot() methods for prevalence, multimorbidity, concentration-index, concentration-curve and pattern results.
  • New vignette vignette("real-data-nhanes") using real NHANES 2009-2010 data.

Changes

  • survey_map_indicator(), survey_xgboost(), survey_shap() and plot_shap_summary() are now labelled experimental.

  • Concentration-index p-values are computed as 2 * pnorm(-|z|) for accuracy with very small values.

  • New simulated example datasets ncd_survey (2,400 adults, STEPS-style raw response codes, stratified two-stage cluster design with unequal weights) and child_anthro (1,034 children with DHS-coded z-scores), drawn from a known synthetic population. Generating code is in data-raw/ of the source repository.

  • New vignette vignette("full-workflow") demonstrating every exported function on the example datasets.

  • survey_concentration_index(): respondents tied on the ranking variable (for example DHS wealth quintiles) now share the mid-point of their group’s cumulative-weight interval. Previously ties were ranked by row order, so the estimate changed when the rows of the input were reordered. Results for untied ranking variables are unchanged.

  • Tests: the replicate-weight validation of the concentration index now uses a tolerance of 1e-8 (the two calculations agree to machine precision); added a tie-invariance regression test and tests for survey_map_indicator() (run when sf is installed).

  • Documentation: README status column now distinguishes tested functions from the exploratory machine-learning module, and a Limitations section was added.

  • Added CONTRIBUTING.md and CITATION.cff; added the author ORCID.

SurveyNCD 0.1.0

CRAN release: 2026-09-28

First release (CRAN 2026-09-28)

  • Initial release officially accepted and published on CRAN (https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=SurveyNCD).
  • recode_binary(): converts raw survey coding (e.g. 1/2/9) to clean 0/1/NA. When no is not specified, non-yes values are treated as 0.
  • multimorbidity_index(): self-reported multimorbidity score based on the Functional Comorbidity Index (Groll et al., 2005, doi:10.1016/j.jclinepi.2004.10.018). Safely handles all-NA respondents.
  • fci_items(): reference list of 18 standard FCI conditions
  • mm_prevalence(): design-weighted population prevalence with logit confidence intervals via the survey package. Includes lonely PSU protection.
  • survey_concentration_index(): survey-weighted concentration index for health inequality analysis with design-consistent standard errors via Kakwani’s convenient regression (Kakwani, Wagstaff, & van Doorslaer, 1997, doi:10.1016/S0304-4076(96)01807-6). Returns full-precision values.
  • who_anthro_score(): WHO severity categorisation for DHS-style anthropometric z-scores with biologically implausible value flagging per WHO child growth standards (WHO, 2006).
  • survey_map_indicator(): choropleth mapping of survey indicators via sf
  • survey_xgboost(): case-weighted gradient boosting for survey data (exploratory)
  • survey_shap(): SHAP feature contributions from survey_xgboost() models
  • plot_shap_summary(): SHAP summary visualisation
